purpose: Pilot private-input predicate. Checks that privately held monthly debt obligations, 16 fixed slots, are at most a chosen share of a privately held monthly income, and publishes only a yes/no verdict. The share comes from a fixed public list (36, 43, 45 or 50 percent) because 12 CFR 1026.51(a)(1)(ii) tells a card issuer to consider the ratio of debt obligations to income in its written policies but names no number. Zero income gives no. Carries an OCG Standard section 25 ocg-private-input@1 declaration: the income and the debts are each committed under sha256-salted@1 with their own independent salt, in policy_parameters.income_commitment and policy_parameters.debts_commitment, so the income can be opened to an employment-verification party without opening the debts. Integer arithmetic only. The witness must be exactly 16 slots of 20-digit amounts so its length does not reveal how many debts exist; any other shape is refused and nothing is sealed. It does not show that every debt was listed, that the income is real or accessible, or the minimum-payment estimate in paragraph (a)(2), and assets are out of scope. The verdict is public and the inputs are not in the receipt; a receipt made from inputs given to a server was seen by that server, and many yes/no questions about the same figures at different shares reveal more than one. Pilot: the node lands with its proof deferred and the in-browser result is a preview, not a receipt.

trust_label: deferred: deterministic source published, zkVM proof not yet generated; New gpu:false private-input node, art-811-check-dti-within-policy-private, authored 2026-11-03. Exec-only measure on the section 25 private-input guest (PRIVATE-PREDICATE-DESIGN-1, prototype of this kernel): MAX 7,295,082 user_cycles over 48 segments, FAST class under the 30M ceiling; proving is the separate PRIVATE-PREDICATE-PROVE-1 row, which needs its SIDEBYSIDE row first (SO #39; the threshold list is CLAUSE-SILENT). Deferred per the section 18 steady-state rule (RIDER-KERNEL.md).
